reference.title: Scenario 2 — List Bullet with bold term and separator pattern
reference.shortdesc: Consider a concept section titled "Connection Modes" where the author has used a bulleted list

section.p: Consider a concept section titled "Connection Modes" where the author has used a bulleted list where each List Bullet paragraph begins with a bold-formatted term followed by a — separator and definition text.

row.entry: [Heading 2]: Connection Modes [Normal]: The device supports the following connection modes. [List Bullet, Bold run: "Wired"] — Uses an Ethernet cable to connect the device directly to the network switch. [List Bullet, Bold run: "Wireless"] — Connects the device using the built-in Wi-Fi adapter. [List Bullet, Bold run: "Bluetooth"] — Pairs the device with a host computer for short-range data transfer.

entry.codeblock:
Connection Modes

The device supports the following connection modes.

Wired

Uses an Ethernet cable to connect the device directly to the network switch.

Wireless

Connects the device using the built-in Wi-Fi adapter.

Bluetooth

Pairs the device with a host computer for short-range data transfer.

section.p: Result: The converter detects the bold-term pattern and maps the List Bullet items to a DITA <dl>. Each list item becomes a <dlentry>, the bold run maps to <dt>, and the remaining text maps to <dd>. The separator character is stripped.
